title: Critical Value Reporting Protocol
content: Laboratory critical values (also called panic values) are results so abnormal they may indicate a life-threatening condition requiring immediate clinical action. The Laboratory must call the critical value directly to the treating physician or responsible nurse within 15 minutes of result verification; the HIS alert must be triggered simultaneously. The caller must document: result, time called, person notified, their acknowledgment, and the read-back confirmation in the LIS. If the responsible clinician cannot be reached within 15 minutes, the call must escalate to the ward charge nurse and then to the Medical Superintendent. Critical value thresholds (e.g., serum potassium <2.5 or >6.5 mmol/L, blood glucose <2.2 or >25 mmol/L, hemoglobin <5 g/dL) are defined in the Lab Critical Value Table maintained by the Laboratory Committee and reviewed annually.
